frozen_original.description_long: CNN’s July 2015 report described historical Trump business dealings with people and firms alleged or documented to have organized-crime ties. It said Trump used S&A Concrete to build Trump Plaza condominiums and cited federal court records, as discussed in journalist Wayne Barrett’s book, identifying Genovese crime-family head Anthony “Fat Tony” Salerno and Gambino leader Paul Castellano as controllers of S&A. The story also recounted a separate Atlantic City property transaction involving Salvatore Testa, attributing details to earlier reporting and Barrett. CNN noted that Trump was a target of a 1979 bribery investigation and was questioned in a 1981 racketeering probe, but neither investigation led to criminal charges. The Washington Post’s 2015 investigation likewise reported that Trump worked with mob-controlled companies and unions in his early development career. These accounts support an attributed description of business relationships and public scrutiny. They do not establish that Trump knowingly joined a criminal enterprise, violated RICO, or conspired with mob figures. The replacement avoids presenting those legal conclusions as findings.
